lines: Captain! Come to hear a song? I know three. Well, two and a half.
Don't look at me like that. No guard, no cell. A free man can sing if he wants to.

options.text: Keep it down. People are trying to sleep.
reply: Sleep? On this wreck? Nobody's sleeping, Captain. They're just lying still and counting the food.

options.text: What were you locked up for?
reply: Ha. Ask me again when we're down to the last ration bar. Then you'll really want to know.
Suit yourself. The half song the best one anyway.

lines: The freezer airlock's sealed tight. I checked it twice this morning. Three times, maybe.

options.text: You saved us when you sealed it.
reply: Daniel was still on the other side. Don't call it saving.
If I close my eyes I hear the fire. Give me something to fix instead.

lines: It's Dr. Voss. I saw you hesitate.
If you're here about the compost bin, my answer hasn't changed.

options.text: We may not have a choice about the food.
reply: There is always a choice. It's usually between dying slowly and dying slightly less slowly.
Physically? Fine. Mentally, Mason is singing and Elias stopped blinking. Draw your own conclusions.

options.text: Sorry to bother you, Dr. Voss.

lines: Oh! Captain. I was just sorting what's left.
It looks worse than it is. Mostly. I can stretch it, I promise. Not a single crumb wasted.

options.text: How long can the Food last?
reply: Depends how many mouths there are to feed. I'd rather not do that math out loud.
Safe enough, if it's cooked hot. Please don't tell Dr. Voss I said that.
Thank me when there's still dinner on Day 30.

lines: Hey, Captain. Pull up some floor. It's the comfiest floor on the ship.
Don't worry about me. I don't need much. Just a little something to rinse with now and then.

options.text: Where did you even come from?
reply: Out there. Drifting. You know how it is. Then I heard your airlock was friendly.

options.text: Are you going to help out around here?
reply: Help? I'm keeping morale up. Look at me. Do I look worried? That's leadership.
